method: COMPILED FROM 2 SOURCES. S1: PARAPHRASED AND HASH-ANCHORED from Infectious Diseases Society of America (Patterson et al.), Oxford University Press 'Practice Guidelines for the Diagnosis and Management of Aspergillosis: 2016 Update by the Infectious Diseases Society of America (Clin Infect Dis 63(4):e1, published online 29 Jun 2016)' (2016), 20 claims; LICENCE: 'This work is written by (a) US Government employee(s) and is in the public domain in the US.' Status outside the US not stated, so paraphrased. (read at permissions statement on the PMC article page PMC4967602 (read 2026-09-23)). S2: PARAPHRASED AND HASH-ANCHORED from Epelbaum O, Marinelli T, Haydour QS, et al., American Thoracic Society, Am J Respir Crit Care Med 211(1):34 (doi 10.1164/rccm.202410-2045ST) 'Treatment of Invasive Pulmonary Aspergillosis and Preventive and Empirical Therapy for Invasive Candidiasis in Adult Pulmonary and Critical Care Patients: An Official American Thoracic Society Clinical Practice Guideline' (2025), 6 claims; LICENCE: Copyright © 2025 by the American Thoracic Society. 'You may print one copy of this document at no charge. However, if you require more than one copy, you must place a reprint order.' (read at Europe PMC fullTextXML <permissions> element for PMC11755356). Verify each source separately: verify.py --source <file> --only-source S<n>. Edition 2.0 adds S2, the ATS 2025 clinical practice guideline, paraphrased and hash-anchored; it answers one aspergillosis question (triazole monotherapy versus triazole plus echinocandin) and states no doses. The S1 claims are unchanged. The Australasian 2021 consensus (Intern Med J, doi 10.1111/imj.15591) was retried on 2026-09-24 and Wiley again returned HTTP 403; Unpaywall lists no open copy. A CC BY German ICU guideline (Infection 2025, PMC12316785) was read but gives no doses in its text and was not used.

claims.claim: **Get a chest CT whenever invasive pulmonary aspergillosis is suspected, even if the chest X-ray is normal** (strong; high). Contrast is not routine, but use it when a nodule or mass lies near a large vessel.
claims.locator: Infectious Diseases Society of America (Patterson et al.), Oxford University Press, 'Practice Guidelines for the Diagnosis and Management of Aspergillosis: 2016 Update by the Infectious Diseases Society of America (Clin Infect Dis 63(4):e1, published online 29 Jun 2016)', 2016, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4967602/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Do bronchoscopy with BAL when IPA is suspected** (strong; moderate), unless severe hypoxaemia, bleeding or refractory thrombocytopenia prevent it. Peripheral nodules yield little on BAL, so consider percutaneous or endobronchial biopsy.
claims.locator: Infectious Diseases Society of America (Patterson et al.), Oxford University Press, 'Practice Guidelines for the Diagnosis and Management of Aspergillosis: 2016 Update by the Infectious Diseases Society of America (Clin Infect Dis 63(4):e1, published online 29 Jun 2016)', 2016, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4967602/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Serum and BAL galactomannan is an accurate marker in haematological malignancy and HSCT** (strong; high). Do not use it for routine blood screening during mould-active therapy or prophylaxis (bronchoscopy samples are still fine), or to screen SOT recipients or people with chronic granulomatous disease.
claims.locator: Infectious Diseases Society of America (Patterson et al.), Oxford University Press, 'Practice Guidelines for the Diagnosis and Management of Aspergillosis: 2016 Update by the Infectious Diseases Society of America (Clin Infect Dis 63(4):e1, published online 29 Jun 2016)', 2016, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4967602/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Serum beta-D-glucan helps in high-risk patients (haematological malignancy, allogeneic HSCT) but is not specific for *Aspergillus*** (strong; moderate).
claims.locator: Infectious Diseases Society of America (Patterson et al.), Oxford University Press, 'Practice Guidelines for the Diagnosis and Management of Aspergillosis: 2016 Update by the Infectious Diseases Society of America (Clin Infect Dis 63(4):e1, published online 29 Jun 2016)', 2016, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4967602/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Voriconazole is the primary treatment** (strong; high). **Start antifungals early when IPA is strongly suspected,** while the work-up continues (strong; high).
claims.locator: Infectious Diseases Society of America (Patterson et al.), Oxford University Press, 'Practice Guidelines for the Diagnosis and Management of Aspergillosis: 2016 Update by the Infectious Diseases Society of America (Clin Infect Dis 63(4):e1, published online 29 Jun 2016)', 2016, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4967602/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Alternatives: liposomal amphotericin B or isavuconazole** (both strong; moderate), or another lipid amphotericin formulation (weak; low).
claims.locator: Infectious Diseases Society of America (Patterson et al.), Oxford University Press, 'Practice Guidelines for the Diagnosis and Management of Aspergillosis: 2016 Update by the Infectious Diseases Society of America (Clin Infect Dis 63(4):e1, published online 29 Jun 2016)', 2016, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4967602/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Voriconazole plus an echinocandin may be considered in selected patients with documented IPA** (weak; moderate). An echinocandin alone is not recommended as primary therapy; keep it for when azoles and polyenes are contraindicated.
claims.locator: Infectious Diseases Society of America (Patterson et al.), Oxford University Press, 'Practice Guidelines for the Diagnosis and Management of Aspergillosis: 2016 Update by the Infectious Diseases Society of America (Clin Infect Dis 63(4):e1, published online 29 Jun 2016)', 2016, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4967602/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Treat for at least 6–12 weeks,** depending on how deep and long the immunosuppression is, the site, and response (strong; low). If immunosuppression must continue after successful treatment, give secondary prophylaxis (strong; moderate).
claims.locator: Infectious Diseases Society of America (Patterson et al.), Oxford University Press, 'Practice Guidelines for the Diagnosis and Management of Aspergillosis: 2016 Update by the Infectious Diseases Society of America (Clin Infect Dis 63(4):e1, published online 29 Jun 2016)', 2016, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4967602/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Cut back or stop immunosuppressive drugs where feasible** as part of treatment (strong; low).
claims.locator: Infectious Diseases Society of America (Patterson et al.), Oxford University Press, 'Practice Guidelines for the Diagnosis and Management of Aspergillosis: 2016 Update by the Infectious Diseases Society of America (Clin Infect Dis 63(4):e1, published online 29 Jun 2016)', 2016, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4967602/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Therapeutic drug monitoring of the azole (itraconazole, voriconazole, posaconazole) once at steady state** during treatment, prolonged prophylaxis or when interactions are expected; also measure interacting drugs such as ciclosporin, tacrolimus and sirolimus.
claims.locator: Infectious Diseases Society of America (Patterson et al.), Oxford University Press, 'Practice Guidelines for the Diagnosis and Management of Aspergillosis: 2016 Update by the Infectious Diseases Society of America (Clin Infect Dis 63(4):e1, published online 29 Jun 2016)', 2016, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4967602/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Repeat the chest CT after at least 2 weeks of treatment** to judge response, sooner if the patient deteriorates (weak; low).
claims.locator: Infectious Diseases Society of America (Patterson et al.), Oxford University Press, 'Practice Guidelines for the Diagnosis and Management of Aspergillosis: 2016 Update by the Infectious Diseases Society of America (Clin Infect Dis 63(4):e1, published online 29 Jun 2016)', 2016, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4967602/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Aspergillosis does not absolutely rule out further chemotherapy or HSCT** (strong; moderate); the timing should be decided jointly by infectious diseases and haematology/oncology.
claims.locator: Infectious Diseases Society of America (Patterson et al.), Oxford University Press, 'Practice Guidelines for the Diagnosis and Management of Aspergillosis: 2016 Update by the Infectious Diseases Society of America (Clin Infect Dis 63(4):e1, published online 29 Jun 2016)', 2016, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4967602/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Salvage options: lipid amphotericin B, micafungin, caspofungin, posaconazole or itraconazole,** choosing a triazole in the light of prior antifungals, host factors, pharmacokinetics and possible resistance (strong; moderate).
claims.locator: Infectious Diseases Society of America (Patterson et al.), Oxford University Press, 'Practice Guidelines for the Diagnosis and Management of Aspergillosis: 2016 Update by the Infectious Diseases Society of America (Clin Infect Dis 63(4):e1, published online 29 Jun 2016)', 2016, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4967602/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **CNS aspergillosis: voriconazole first,** with lipid amphotericin B only for those intolerant of or failing it (strong; moderate).
claims.locator: Infectious Diseases Society of America (Patterson et al.), Oxford University Press, 'Practice Guidelines for the Diagnosis and Management of Aspergillosis: 2016 Update by the Infectious Diseases Society of America (Clin Infect Dis 63(4):e1, published online 29 Jun 2016)', 2016, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4967602/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **For proven or probable invasive pulmonary aspergillosis, S2 accepts either a mould-active triazole alone or a triazole plus an echinocandin as first treatment** (conditional; low-quality evidence); the evidence could not separate the two.
claims.locator: Epelbaum O, Marinelli T, Haydour QS, et al., American Thoracic Society, Am J Respir Crit Care Med 211(1):34 (doi 10.1164/rccm.202410-2045ST), 'Treatment of Invasive Pulmonary Aspergillosis and Preventive and Empirical Therapy for Invasive Candidiasis in Adult Pulmonary and Critical Care Patients: An Official American Thoracic Society Clinical Practice Guideline', 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11755356/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Lean towards the combination in the critically ill, when triazole resistance is a worry, and when the diagnosis rests on a positive galactomannan** (serum or BAL). The data come only from haematological malignancy and stem cell transplant patients, so use in other groups is uncertain.
claims.locator: Epelbaum O, Marinelli T, Haydour QS, et al., American Thoracic Society, Am J Respir Crit Care Med 211(1):34 (doi 10.1164/rccm.202410-2045ST), 'Treatment of Invasive Pulmonary Aspergillosis and Preventive and Empirical Therapy for Invasive Candidiasis in Adult Pulmonary and Critical Care Patients: An Official American Thoracic Society Clinical Practice Guideline', 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11755356/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Posaconazole and isavuconazole are now often used first line instead of voriconazole** (similar efficacy, steadier drug levels, fewer side effects), and S2 extends its advice to them although the trials used voriconazole. Rezafungin, with its very long half-life, is not interchangeable with micafungin or anidulafungin.
claims.locator: Epelbaum O, Marinelli T, Haydour QS, et al., American Thoracic Society, Am J Respir Crit Care Med 211(1):34 (doi 10.1164/rccm.202410-2045ST), 'Treatment of Invasive Pulmonary Aspergillosis and Preventive and Empirical Therapy for Invasive Candidiasis in Adult Pulmonary and Critical Care Patients: An Official American Thoracic Society Clinical Practice Guideline', 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11755356/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Why combine:** voriconazole has resistance that may not extend to other azoles, very variable levels (often below target despite loading), and can miss mixed infections such as *Aspergillus* with Mucorales. All trial comparisons were voriconazole with or without micafungin or anidulafungin.
claims.locator: Epelbaum O, Marinelli T, Haydour QS, et al., American Thoracic Society, Am J Respir Crit Care Med 211(1):34 (doi 10.1164/rccm.202410-2045ST), 'Treatment of Invasive Pulmonary Aspergillosis and Preventive and Empirical Therapy for Invasive Candidiasis in Adult Pulmonary and Critical Care Patients: An Official American Thoracic Society Clinical Practice Guideline', 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11755356/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Azole resistance in clinical *A. fumigatus*:** about 3.2% in Europe and 1.4% in the United States, above 10% in some countries; international and European guidance already favours starting a combination where environmental resistance exceeds 10%. Susceptibility testing of the patient's own isolate may then allow a step down to the triazole alone.
claims.locator: Epelbaum O, Marinelli T, Haydour QS, et al., American Thoracic Society, Am J Respir Crit Care Med 211(1):34 (doi 10.1164/rccm.202410-2045ST), 'Treatment of Invasive Pulmonary Aspergillosis and Preventive and Empirical Therapy for Invasive Candidiasis in Adult Pulmonary and Critical Care Patients: An Official American Thoracic Society Clinical Practice Guideline', 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11755356/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Check the neutrophil count when choosing between one and two drugs.** How long to continue a combination, and when to step down to one drug, are not established.
claims.locator: Epelbaum O, Marinelli T, Haydour QS, et al., American Thoracic Society, Am J Respir Crit Care Med 211(1):34 (doi 10.1164/rccm.202410-2045ST), 'Treatment of Invasive Pulmonary Aspergillosis and Preventive and Empirical Therapy for Invasive Candidiasis in Adult Pulmonary and Critical Care Patients: An Official American Thoracic Society Clinical Practice Guideline', 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11755356/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **In prolonged neutropenia at high risk of IA, give prophylaxis with posaconazole (strong; high), voriconazole (strong; moderate) or micafungin (weak; low).** Itraconazole works but is limited by absorption and tolerability. Do not combine triazoles with drugs that become toxic alongside them, such as vinca alkaloids.
claims.locator: Infectious Diseases Society of America (Patterson et al.), Oxford University Press, 'Practice Guidelines for the Diagnosis and Management of Aspergillosis: 2016 Update by the Infectious Diseases Society of America (Clin Infect Dis 63(4):e1, published online 29 Jun 2016)', 2016, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4967602/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Posaconazole prophylaxis for allogeneic HSCT recipients with GVHD at high risk of IA** (strong; high), continued for as long as the GVHD-related immunosuppression lasts (for example prednisone equivalent above 1 mg/kg/day for over 2 weeks).
claims.locator: Infectious Diseases Society of America (Patterson et al.), Oxford University Press, 'Practice Guidelines for the Diagnosis and Management of Aspergillosis: 2016 Update by the Infectious Diseases Society of America (Clin Infect Dis 63(4):e1, published online 29 Jun 2016)', 2016, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4967602/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **After lung transplant, give 3 to 4 months of antifungal prophylaxis** with a systemic triazole (voriconazole or itraconazole) or inhaled amphotericin B (strong; moderate).
claims.locator: Infectious Diseases Society of America (Patterson et al.), Oxford University Press, 'Practice Guidelines for the Diagnosis and Management of Aspergillosis: 2016 Update by the Infectious Diseases Society of America (Clin Infect Dis 63(4):e1, published online 29 Jun 2016)', 2016, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4967602/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Empiric antifungals for high-risk patients with prolonged neutropenia and persistent fever despite broad-spectrum antibiotics:** a lipid amphotericin B or an echinocandin (caspofungin, micafungin) (strong; high), or voriconazole. Not when neutropenia is expected to last under 10 days, unless other findings point to invasive fungal infection.
claims.locator: Infectious Diseases Society of America (Patterson et al.), Oxford University Press, 'Practice Guidelines for the Diagnosis and Management of Aspergillosis: 2016 Update by the Infectious Diseases Society of America (Clin Infect Dis 63(4):e1, published online 29 Jun 2016)', 2016, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4967602/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Treat chronic cavitary pulmonary aspergillosis with at least 6 months of antifungals when there are symptoms or declining lung function or imaging** (strong; low); asymptomatic, stable patients can be observed and reviewed every 3–6 months.
claims.locator: Infectious Diseases Society of America (Patterson et al.), Oxford University Press, 'Practice Guidelines for the Diagnosis and Management of Aspergillosis: 2016 Update by the Infectious Diseases Society of America (Clin Infect Dis 63(4):e1, published online 29 Jun 2016)', 2016, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4967602/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Oral itraconazole or voriconazole are the preferred agents** (strong; high); posaconazole is a third-line choice after adverse effects or failure (strong; moderate).
claims.locator: Infectious Diseases Society of America (Patterson et al.), Oxford University Press, 'Practice Guidelines for the Diagnosis and Management of Aspergillosis: 2016 Update by the Infectious Diseases Society of America (Clin Infect Dis 63(4):e1, published online 29 Jun 2016)', 2016, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4967602/, retrieved 2026-09-23
